module0.title: Why Should You Care?
module0.subtitle: Understanding the Significance of Navier-Stokes
module0.description: Explore real-world applications and the historical significance of the Navier-Stokes equations.
module0.content: The Navier-Stokes equations govern how fluids move in response to forces. From weather prediction to aircraft design, these equations are fundamental to science and engineering.

module1.title: Fluids as Continuous Mediums
module1.subtitle: From Molecules to Continuum Mechanics
module1.description: Understand how we model fluids as continuous fields rather than discrete particles.
module1.content: Fluids can be described at each point in space by their velocity and pressure. This module introduces the concept of velocity fields and how we interpret them visually.

module2.title: Forces & Acceleration
module2.subtitle: Newton's Second Law Applied to Fluids
module2.description: Learn how forces act on fluids to produce acceleration.
module2.content: Three primary forces act on fluid elements: pressure gradients push from high to low pressure, viscosity provides internal friction, and body forces like gravity pull downward.

module3.title: Pressure: The Dominant Force
module3.subtitle: Pressure Gradients and Incompressibility
module3.description: Explore how pressure drives fluid flow.
module3.content: Pressure gradients (∇p) are one of the most important driving forces in fluid dynamics. In incompressible flows, mass is conserved at every point (∇·u = 0).

module4.title: Viscosity & Friction
module4.subtitle: Internal Resistance in Fluids
module4.description: Understand how viscosity creates resistance and dissipates energy.
module4.content: Viscosity (μ) represents internal friction. Different fluids have different viscosities: honey is thick (high μ), water is moderate, air is thin (low μ).

module5.title: The Complete Equation
module5.subtitle: Putting It All Together
module5.description: See how all terms combine into the Navier-Stokes momentum equation.
module5.content: The complete Navier-Stokes equation: ρ(∂u/∂t + u·∇u) = -∇p + μ∇²u + ρg describes how fluids accelerate in response to all forces acting upon them.
